title: Cohort-based control-plane version promotion for VPC private deployments
creator: Aisha Mendez
description: Implement a cohort-based promotion system for control-plane version upgrades targeting VPC/private deployments. Goal is to provide a safer, automated alternative to single-host canaries that: (1) creates isolated cohorts of customers/nodes for early verification; (2) integrates with Terraform modules so upgrades are declarative; (3) uses health and behavioral gates to automatically promote or rollback; and (4) emits clear telemetry to Console for SRE/PM visibility.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy and promote a new control-plane version to a <1% production cohort in at least two VPCs using the new Terraform module
Health gates (p95 latency, 5xx rate, KV cache hit ratio, control-plane error budget) are evaluated automatically and can block promotion
Automated rollback completes within configured SLA (<5 minutes) when gates fail during promotion
Promotion window and cohort size are configurable via Terraform variables and Console overrides
Audit trail recorded in control-plane logs + customer audit log for each promotion event
No change to existing private control-plane API surface for customers; rollout is transparent and reversible
implementation_steps: Design a CohortController component in control-plane that can target node groups by tag/label and orchestrate version promotes/rollbacks
Add Terraform module changes: private/controlplane/upgrade with variables for cohort_size_pct, cohort_selector, promotion_schedule, health_gate thresholds
Implement a promotion engine with state machine: staged -> measuring -> promoted -> stable, including timed pauses and retry limits
Wire telemetry hooks: emit 'promotion_event', 'gate_eval', and per-cohort metrics to existing observability pipeline
Create a synchronous API endpoint for Console to trigger manual promotions and emergency rollbacks (RBAC-protected)
Build safety checks: preflight compatibility tests, CRD version checks, DB migration dry-run (if any) before cohort kickoff
Write end-to-end tests in infra repo that simulate traffic patterns and force gate failures to validate rollback
terraform_changes: Expose variables: cohort_size_pct (int), cohort_tags (map), promotion_strategy ("cohort"/"blue-green"), health_gates (map)
Add resource: aws/azurerm tags for cohort affinity in node pools
State migration documentation: how to opt-in existing stacks to the new module
Example usage: root module snippet for ops teams to enable cohort promotion
metrics_and_gates: Primary gates: p95 request latency increase < +20% over baseline, 5xx rate < 0.5% absolute, kv_cache_hit_ratio not decreased by more than 5%
Secondary gate: control-plane error budget burn rate < 2x baseline during promotion window
Measurement window: default 10 minutes per stage, configurable per release
Require minimum traffic floor for cohort to be considered valid (e.g., >= 1000 requests/min aggregated)
test_plan: Unit tests for CohortController state transitions
Integration tests: TerraTest scenarios applying module to a sandbox VPC and running simulated workloads
Chaos test: inject latency and errors into a cohort to validate rollback path
Staging end-to-end: run promotion against staging fleet with synthetic and production-like traffic and verify metrics emitted to Console
Security review: threat-model new API endpoints and ensure KMS-wrapped secrets are not leaked during rollout
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback is triggered when any critical gate trips or when manual abort is called via Console/CLI. Rollback sequence: mark cohort as 'rollback', drain new control-plane pods from cohort nodes, reassign traffic back to previous version, validate gate metrics return to baseline, mark cohort stable. Emergency rollback shortcut returns all cohorts to previous version and opens incident ticket automatically.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: cohort traffic too small to evaluate regressions -> Mitigation: enforce minimum traffic floor and allow federation of cohorts across regions
Risk: Terraform state drift between on-prem and cloud deployments -> Mitigation: state-migration docs and preflight drift detection
Risk: slow rollback on DB or schema incompatible changes -> Mitigation: require migration feature flags and non-destructive migrations with canary toggles
Risk: operator error in cohort selection -> Mitigation: RBAC + guarded Console flows + dry-run option
docs_and_communication: Announcement template for customers: ops@redwood-inference.com - include rollout schedule, opt-out instructions, and support contacts
